content:
The docstring of docs#lim refers to itself as Filter.lim, but docs#Filter.lim does not exist. Was this intended to be named as Filter.lim?

The same goes for docs#limUnder, although this one refers to itself properly in its docstring.
Yes, they are both missing their namespace. Please open a PR ! :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:
After running a lake build, it seems that the proof of docs#MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.limUnder refers to limUnder as _root_.limUnder which might suggest it was intentional.
That's merely because otherwise limUnder would refer to MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.limUnder itself. The better solution would be to make this lemma protected

I used the script scripts/add_deprecation.sh to add deprecation aliases, like @[deprecated (since := "2026-03-12")] alias lim := Filter.lim. But many files in mathlib open Filter and then refer to lim, and the alias makes it an ambiguous definition, which causes CI to fail. I could mark Filter.lim as protected but this would require changing much of mathlib, and I don't think it should be protected. What should I do?
I was afraid you'd run into that, yeah. What do you think the best outcome would be after deprecation - should lim always be written Filter.lim or not?
Can you export Filter (lim) so that at least the full name is Filter.lim, even if for now it remains in the root namespace?
how would we signal that Filter.lim being in the root namespace is deprecated
I'm not sure; I'm proposing that we ignore that problem for now and at least give it the right name in the docs
Probably theres an RFC here for deprecated export

I was afraid you'd run into that, yeah. What do you think the best outcome would be after deprecation - should lim always be written Filter.lim or not?

I think actually most of the time it should be written with dot notation as f.lim

It is unclear if this means we should make Filter.lim protected though. I mean docs#List.append and docs#Array.append are protected, but some functions which are primarily queried through dot notation, e.g. docs#LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues, aren't.

To be honest the fact that we had to make List.append and Array.append protected in the first place is a little bit concerning to me, because in my view having to make all function names like append either globally unique or protected largely defeats the purpose of having namespaces in the first place. This could be seen as something the importer should take responsibility for. But I suppose that's a topic for another thread.

Edit: I opened another thread #lean4 > Adding definitions breaks backwards compatibility to discuss this because it doesn't have much to do with lim vs Filter.lim
In this case, simply drop the deprecation
I reverted the commit to add the deprecation. I can alternatively mark Filter.lim as protected and use dot notation for most of mathlib, if this is preferred.
